clinical_profiles.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

patient_info.stressor: Sara began a part-time MBA prerequisite program while continuing her operations role at the startup, seeing it as the next logical step toward leading larger teams and eventually studying tech hubs abroad. During the next two months, the combination of coursework, startup deadlines, networking events, and volleyball commitments coincided with a sustained surge in energy, faster speech, racing strategy ideas, and unusually expansive plans for reorganizing both school and work systems. Her fixed beliefs about certain classmates and stakeholders having a special role in her career, along with vivid perceptions that felt real to her, began to interfere with meetings and group projects despite her still trying to keep up appearances. After a professor questioned her judgment on a team assignment and her manager documented a clear drop in work reliability, Sara used the company EAP to arrange an outpatient psychiatric assessment.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I came in because I know this sounds hard to explain, but I’ve been completely convinced that one of my MBA classmates and a startup advisor are quietly coordinating opportunities for me, like certain comments in class or Slack messages are coded signals about where my career is supposed to go.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: A few times a week, usually when I’m working late on school or operations plans, I hear my name or a short phrase like 'go now' so clearly that I check my phone or look around the room even though no one is there.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Most days I’ve felt unusually switched on and optimistic, like I’m right on the edge of something huge, but I also snap at teammates or my boyfriend over small delays that normally wouldn’t bother me.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I’ve had this constant motor running in me where I go from work dashboards to class readings to volleyball scheduling without wanting to pause, and sitting through a normal meeting feels almost physically uncomfortable.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: People keep telling me I’m talking too fast in meetings and study groups, and I notice I’ll keep explaining my ideas even after someone tries to jump in because silence feels like I’m losing momentum.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My mind has been jumping from market expansion to coursework to org charts to moving abroad so quickly that I’ll open five documents and forget which idea I was trying to capture first.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: I’ve been launching extra work projects, rewriting team processes for class, messaging contacts from networking events, and trying to organize everyone’s schedules, even though some of it has made me miss normal follow-through on my actual tasks.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Before this stretch of being so energized and driven, I never had messages feel coded like this or heard my name when no one was there. Those experiences only started once my mood and workload intensity shifted after beginning the MBA prerequisites.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My manager has started documenting missed handoffs and unreliable follow-through, and my professor questioned my judgment on a group assignment. I’m still showing up, but my work and school relationships are getting strained enough that I felt I needed help.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about two months, since I started the part-time MBA prerequisite program while keeping my operations job.
